from_notes: The foundation cream used by the Satavahana dancers was known as Aradalam
from_notes_src: NextGen AP History Previous Papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt) p.13
x: No option is right: Maiputa (Telugu maipoota) is the dancers' foundation cream, which NextGen and Rocket call Aradalam. The old key Kusuma Lepanam came from a wrong PYQ key; Kumkuma Tilakam, Gajjelu and Mridangam are not creams.
source: NextGen AP History Previous Papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt) p.13; src/ap-history/rocket-ap-history.txt

from_notes: Women participated equally with men in festivals and gatherings. They donated generously to Buddhist Viharas and Chaityas.
x: Defective question: inscriptions support three options at once – women were prominent (titles such as Mahabhojaki, Mahasenapatni), donated lavishly to viharas and chaityas, and kings bore matronymics (Gautamiputra, Vasishthiputra). Only option 4 is plainly false, since polygamy was practised in the upper classes; with no 'all of these' option no single key can be given.
evidence: NextGen Satavahanas (src/ap-history/nextgen-03-satavahanas.txt) p.15 (polygamy in upper classes; women donated; husbands' titles)

x: Samudragupta is the first Gupta styled Paramabhagavata, in his Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (NextGen Rocket); Chandragupta II used it regularly on coins and inscriptions, which is why some keys give him.
source: Rocket Indian History Part 1 (src/indian-history/rocket-indian-history-01.txt) (Samudragupta – Param Bhagavata)

dispute: Most books and the UPPSC official key give Chandragupta II, who used 'Parama Bhagavata' widely on coins and inscriptions. The NextGen Rocket Sheet gives Samudragupta, styled so in the Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (whose genuineness is doubted).

x: The Nalanda and Gaya copper plates style Samudragupta Paramabhagavata, making him the first Gupta with the title (NextGen Rocket). The official UPPSC key gave Chandragupta II, who used it widely on coins.
